_about: Routing lines that replace a skill's own description in Jev's skill index (jev-refine.py, routing_overrides). Format: stage | project fit | needs | model | tie-breaker | not for. Researched 2026-10-05 from each SKILL.md in full plus upstream READMEs. Max 500 chars each.

skills.impeccable: DEFAULT design skill. Stage: any (build, redesign, critique, audit, polish, animate, document). Fits every UI incl. SaaS apps, dashboards, landing, docs, portfolio, native iOS/Android. Keeps project memory (PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md), 24 commands, live browser loop. Needs Node, browser for verification, strong model. Pick unless the user names another skill or asks only for references, a recipe look, or a read-only plan.
skills.refero-design: Stage: reference research before building. Pulls real styles, screens and flows from the Refero MCP, locks one primary reference, writes a decision ledger, then builds. Fits web marketing/product pages (styles) and web/iOS app flows (screens). Needs Refero MCP. Use when the user asks how other products do it, for inspiration, or to ground a design in shipped work. Not for polish or projects with a fixed design system.
skills.mobbin-search: Stage: reference lookup only (no build method). Searches Mobbin for real iOS/web app screens and flows, answers with links or an HTML evidence board. Needs Mobbin MCP and a vision model; light model fine. Pick for 'how do other apps handle login/onboarding/checkout' or when Mobbin is named. Prefer refero-design when references should drive a full build; not for marketing-site visual style.
skills.hallmark: Stage: greenfield page build; also audit, redesign, study (extract design DNA from a URL/screenshot). Fits landing, marketing, editorial, portfolio, brand/e-commerce pages and single components; weak for dashboards and app UI. Rotates 21 macrostructures and themes, asks 3 questions first, 58-gate slop test. Strong long-context model. Not the default builder (impeccable is): pick only when Hallmark is named, the user wants rotating structural variety, or 'study this site'.
skills.design-taste-frontend: Stage: greenfield build or redesign of landing pages, portfolios, agency and editorial sites. NOT dashboards, data tables, wizards or native mobile. Sets three dials (variance, motion, density) from the brief and maps briefs to real design systems (Material, Fluent, shadcn...). Defaults React/Next + Tailwind v4 + Motion/GSAP; uses image generation if available. Strong long-context model. Not the default builder (impeccable is): pick when taste-skill is named or dials are wanted.
skills.gpt-taste: Fixed recipe, greenfield only: GSAP-maximal award-style marketing page with pseudo-random layout pick, AIDA structure, 2-line H1 rule, gapless bento, mandatory pinning and scrubbing. React + Tailwind + GSAP. Written for GPT/Codex (stricter taste-skill variant). Pick only when gpt-taste is named or a heavy-GSAP Awwwards recipe is explicitly wanted. Not for restrained, accessibility-critical or design-system work.
skills.high-end-visual-design: Fixed look recipe: glassy 'expensive agency' style (double-bezel cards, floating glass pill nav, spring physics, huge whitespace). Greenfield landing pages for premium SaaS/AI, luxury, real estate, wellness. React/Tailwind + Framer Motion. Pick only when the chosen direction is premium glass/soft luxury. Opposite of minimalist-ui; not for dashboards, minimal or brutalist briefs, or low-end mobile.
skills.minimalist-ui: Fixed look recipe: Notion/Linear-style warm monochrome editorial UI (bone canvas, 1px borders, flat, serif hero, pastel tags, no gradients or pills). Fits workspace/productivity SaaS, docs, notes, calm product marketing, portfolios. Any model. Pick when the chosen direction is minimal or document-like. Not for vivid, glassy, motion-heavy or brutalist briefs.
skills.industrial-brutalist-ui: Fixed look recipe: Swiss print (light) or tactical terminal/CRT (dark) brutalism, no border-radius, hazard-red accent, extreme type scale, ASCII/halftone/scanline details. Fits data-heavy dashboards, portfolios and editorial sites meant to feel like blueprints. Any model. Pick when the direction is brutalist, Swiss, industrial or HUD. Not for friendly consumer, wellness or trust-first commerce.
skills.build-awwwards-quality-sites: Motion and asset layer for greenfield cinematic sites: GSAP + exactly one smooth-scroll engine (Lenis or Locomotive), optional Three.js shaders, generated or licensed imagery, honest logos/avatars, art-direction brief before code. Marketing, editorial, portfolio. Needs strong model, image generation, browser QA. Pair with impeccable for direction. Not for ordinary landing pages, product UI or tight perf budgets.
skills.frontend-design:frontend-design: Anthropic's minimal original: pick one bold aesthetic tone and write distinctive frontend code, no process. Greenfield components/pages, any stack, ~3KB so any model. Pick only for a quick one-off when no project memory, audit or redesign rules are needed; impeccable supersedes it for real projects.
skills.animation-systems: Stage: polish or motion planning. Product-grade motion tokens in Stripe/Linear/Apple/Vercel style (durations, easing, stagger, choreography, reduced motion) delivered as a plan plus a small code recipe. Library-agnostic, any model. Pick to add restrained motion to an existing UI. Not for full page design, GSAP debugging (gsap), jank (fixing-motion-performance) or 3D.
skills.redesign-existing-projects: Stage: redesign of an existing site/app, edits code. Imposes a 'premium' taste-skill look via a long checklist (swap Inter, off-black, one accent, break 3-card rows, grain, spring motion) in the current stack. Fits marketing sites, landings, portfolios, SaaS UI; weak for dense dashboards. Pick when the user wants a premium restyle and accepts a new look. Not when art direction must be preserved (use no-ai-design-slop) or read-only review.
skills.baseline-ui: Stage: fast polish pass, mechanical. Enforces MUST/NEVER rules on React + Tailwind UI (spacing, hierarchy, type, h-dvh, one accent, no gradients, no animation unless asked); '/baseline-ui <file>' reports violations. Small/cheap model fine, no vision. Pick for a quick deslop of Tailwind components. Not for motion-led, gradient or WebGL designs, non-Tailwind stacks, or taste critique.
skills.improve-ui: Stage: read-only audit, never edits product code. Checks one surface against the repo's own design evidence (DESIGN.md, tokens, components), max 3 proven findings, then writes self-contained plans in design-plans/ for another agent. Needs a real repo with a design system; strong long-context model. Pick for design-system drift audits and handoff plans. Not for fixes now, taste critique or accessibility.
skills.no-ai-design-slop: Stage: passive quality gate during building or revising any UI; edits code. Removes reflexive generic defaults and UI defects while preserving the chosen art direction (removal test, one focal point per viewport); prescribes no font or palette. Wants rendered output to verify; strong model. Pick alongside builds or for an anti-slop cleanup that keeps the look. For a read-only review use audit-ai-design-slop.
skills.audit-ai-design-slop: Stage: read-only audit, no edits. Reviews screenshots, rendered pages, mockups or design code for AI clichés and UI defects; returns 5-8 P0-P3 findings with removal-first fixes and unknowns. Vision helps; strong model. Pick for 'does this look AI-generated / anti-slop review'. Not for fixing (no-ai-design-slop), design-system drift (improve-ui), usability critique (uxai:design-critic) or accessibility.
skills.uxai:design-critic: Stage: read-only UX critique. Routes to UX+AI connector methods (heuristic critique, clarity check, cognitive load, consistency, accessibility quick pass, devil's advocate) and returns issues ranked by user cost, each with a fix. Any product type; screenshot, flow or set of screens. Needs the UX+AI connector; vision helps. Pick for usability critique. Not for code changes or AI-slop taste reviews.
skills.uxai:project-health-check: Stage: pre-launch or post-change check of a built project, read-only. Runs UX+AI connector methods in order: ship-readiness QA, security and secrets pass, regression guard; returns a ranked fix list. Not a design skill. Needs the UX+AI connector and repo access. Pick for 'is this ready to go live', 'did I leave keys in', 'will this change break something'. Not for live bugs or visual critique.
skills.landing-page: Stage: plan and copy for a single-offer landing page (one audience, one CTA): outline, hero copy, benefits, how it works, proof, FAQ, SEO/AEO, layout type. Text only, any model; a build skill does the visuals. Pick for conversion structure and copy of SaaS/app/service pages. Not for homepages, visual polish, or critique of an existing page.
skills.webgl-landing-steering: Stage: planning before code. Chooses one WebGL lane for a landing hero (subtle depth, data/particles, 3D object, cinematic) and sets message, performance, accessibility and reliability gates with a fallback-first build order. Three.js projects; any model to plan. Pick for 'WebGL/3D hero that still converts'. Not for pages without WebGL, general cleanup, or full 3D games.
skills.stitch-design-taste: Stage: spec for Google Stitch. Writes a DESIGN.md in Stitch's semantic format that enforces taste-skill's anti-generic rules (one accent, no Inter, no centered hero) for NEW designs. Any model. Pick only when the user works in Google Stitch. To document an existing UI use create-design-md (validated) or firecrawl-website-design-clone (fast).
skills.create-design-md: Stage: documentation of an existing product. Reverse-engineers a validated DESIGN.md from a repo or rendered public URL with evidence for every token, lint and export via @google/design.md; edits only DESIGN.md. Needs Node and browser access; strong model. Pick when accuracy matters or a repo exists. For a quick clone-style extraction from one URL use firecrawl-website-design-clone; inside an impeccable project use impeccable document.
skills.firecrawl-website-design-clone: Stage: fast extraction from one public URL. Two Firecrawl scrapes (branding + images, full-page screenshot) become an agent-ready DESIGN.md meant to clone or be inspired by the site. Needs FIRECRAWL_API_KEY; light model fine. Pick for 'build something in the style of X / extract this site's design'. Not for validated specs (create-design-md), login-gated apps or multi-product references.
skills.design-first-ui-prompting: Stage: prompt writing. A short fill-in template (goal, format, layout, type, color, imagery, exact copy, constraints, negative prompt) for getting consistent output from an image or UI generator, one variable per variant. No tools, any model. Pick to write a prompt for a hero, slide or single screen. Not a build, research or design-system skill; imagegen-frontend-web/mobile are the detailed versions.
skills.image-to-code: Stage: greenfield build, image-first. Generates one large design image per section, analyzes them, then codes the site to match. Fits marketing, landing, portfolio, editorial. Needs an image generator plus strong vision; written for Codex (in Claude use an image MCP). Pick when the user wants to mock up visually then build. Not without image generation, for small edits, or when references or a design system already exist.
skills.imagegen-frontend-web: Stage: concept comps, images only, no code. Generates one horizontal image per website section (hero variety, consistent palette, anti-slop rules) for landing, marketing, e-commerce, agency and portfolio sites. Needs image generation. Pick when the user wants website mockups or design comps. For mockup-then-code use image-to-code; for mobile apps use imagegen-frontend-mobile.
skills.imagegen-frontend-mobile: Stage: concept comps, images only, no code. Generates app-native iOS/Android screens and flows in phone mockups with a consistent app design bible. Needs image generation; capable model. Pick to invent mobile app screens or onboarding flows. Not for websites, building, or real shipped-app references (use mobbin-search).
skills.idea-studio: Stage: earliest ideation, before any design direction. Opens a creative concept, brand concept or product/website idea into concepts, collisions, five lenses and open questions; exploration only, no plan or recommendation. Strong writer model; uses the visualize widget if present. Pick for 'help me think through this idea'. Not for strategy, research synthesis, specs or building.
skills.design:design-critique: Stage: read-only critique at any design stage, lightweight generic checklist (first impression, usability, hierarchy, consistency, basic accessibility, what works, top 3 fixes). Works from a Figma link, screenshot or description; Figma connector optional; vision helps; any model. Pick for quick general feedback on a mockup or Figma frame. For method-driven usability ranking use uxai:design-critic; for AI-slop taste use audit-ai-design-slop.
skills.design:accessibility-review: Stage: read-only WCAG 2.1 AA audit of a design or page before handoff: contrast table, keyboard order, touch targets, screen-reader table, severity-ranked fixes. Figma link, URL or description; any model. Pick to audit accessibility of a design or mockup. To fix accessibility in code use fixing-accessibility.
skills.design:design-handoff: Stage: handoff, design to engineering. Writes a developer spec from a Figma frame or description: layout, tokens, component props, all states, breakpoints, edge cases, motion, accessibility. Figma connector optional; any model. Pick when a finished design needs a spec for developers. Not for building, critique or documenting a whole system.
skills.design:design-system: Stage: design-system work in three modes: audit (naming, hardcoded values, token coverage, scored), document (one component's variants, props, states, a11y) or extend (propose a new component fitting the system). Figma or knowledge-base connectors optional; any model. Pick for component docs or proposing a new pattern. For evidence-gated drift audits with fix plans use improve-ui; for a full DESIGN.md use create-design-md.
skills.design:research-synthesis: Stage: research analysis. Turns interview transcripts, survey results, usability notes, support tickets or NPS into themes with quotes, insight-to-opportunity table, segments and prioritized recommendations. Any model, text input. Pick when raw research data needs distilling. Not for planning research (design:user-research) or design critique.
skills.design:user-research: Stage: research planning. Chooses methods (interviews, usability tests, surveys, card sorts, diary studies, A/B) and drafts research plans and interview guides. Short generic reference, any model. Pick for 'plan a user study / write an interview guide'. For synthesizing collected data use design:research-synthesis.
skills.design:ux-copy: Stage: copy writing or review for interface text: CTAs, error messages, empty states, confirmation dialogs, tooltips, onboarding, with three tone alternatives and localization notes. Any model. Pick for 'what should this button/error/empty state say'. Not for marketing landing-page copy (landing-page).
skills.2ca4e30e-2482-4c94-8644-6c26adf27391:fro: Stage: build/redesign, aesthetic direction only (type, colour, avoiding templated looks). Fits any web UI. No tools needed. Lighter overlap of impeccable: never the default; use only when the user names frontend-design. Not for audits, references or project memory (impeccable), nor fixed recipe looks.
skills.3d3808fa-4d51-4b12-a37a-be06845ed5f3:21s: Stage: build, component sourcing. Installs or generates React/Tailwind components from 21st.dev (pricing table, navbar, hero) and brand logos as SVG. Needs a React+Tailwind project and network. Use when the user wants a ready-made component or a logo; for designing a surface use impeccable. Not for non-React projects or design review.
skills.5398138d-0525-4774-a5f9-063565694c3d:sup: Stage: exploration on the Superdesign canvas: variants across AI models, decks, posters, flows. Needs the Superdesign service/login. Use when the user names Superdesign or wants side-by-side model variants on a canvas. Not the default for building or polishing code UI (impeccable), nor for mockups placed in the real app (build those directly).
skills.69ddeac4-83ae-4467-92f5-0efd884f1f9e:ref: Same as refero-design (synced copy). Stage: reference research before building, via the Refero MCP. Use only when the user asks for references first ('how do others do this', 'find references'). Not the default for building, redesigning or polishing: that is impeccable, even though this skill's description claims to be primary.
skills.music: Stage: build/audio. Generates ElevenLabs Eleven Music (music_v2_5) via API; needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in env or project .env AND a paid plan (free plan returns HTTP 402). For video/reels: use a composition plan (chunks: [Label] + {cues} only, no 'silence' wording), then fit the take to the film's beat grid. Prompt mode may ignore music_length_ms. Tie-breaker: user names ElevenLabs or wants produced music; motion-reel's synthesized score otherwise. Not for SFX or voice.
skills.sound-effects: Stage: build/audio. ElevenLabs SFX via API (needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY). Use when the user asks for ElevenLabs or realistic recorded-style effects; the motion-reel pipeline synthesizes its own SFX with no key, so prefer that for reels unless asked. Not for music (music) or speech (text-to-speech).
skills.update-skills-from-changelog: ElevenLabs maintainer workflow only: updates the elevenlabs/skills repo from an elevenlabs-dx changelog and opens a PR there. Not for any user project work, audio generation or skill installs.
skills.db3da14f-172d-4664-8b03-9ba55af6f95a~g2:: Stage: review and edit. Project fit: the user own local app, dev server (localhost), or local HTML file where code gets edited. Required tools: in-browser inspection. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs lux-web: if a localhost or local file is involved, use lux; external or third-party sites go to lux-web. Not for: external websites, online articles, competitor pages.

Stage: teardown and explanation, read-only. Project fit: external, third-party or competitor websites and online articles with no local codebase. Required tools: in-browser inspection. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs lux: lux is for the users own app and local files that get edited; lux-web is for remote pages only. Not for: user-hosted apps, localhost, local HTML files.
skills.figma~g2:figma-code-connect: Stage: handoff, mapping. Project fit: a codebase with components to link to Figma. Required tools: Figma MCP, Code Connect files (.figma.ts or .figma.js). Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-design-to-code: this one writes the mapping files; design-to-code implements a design as code. Not for: building screens, diagrams, or new Figma files.
skills.figma~g2:figma-create-new-file: Stage: setup. Project fit: any new Figma Design, FigJam, or Slides file is needed. Required tools: Figma MCP create_new_file, load this skill before that call. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker: use this only to create the empty file; content goes to figma-generate-design, figma-use-figjam or figma-use-slides. Not for: editing existing files.
skills.figma~g2:figma-design-to-code: Stage: build from design. Project fit: a codebase that should match a Figma design. Required tools: Figma MCP get_design_context, load this skill first. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-swiftui: use swiftui for iOS, Swift, or SwiftUI targets; use this for web and other code. Motion in the design goes to figma-implement-motion. Not for: pushing code into Figma (figma-generate-design does that).
skills.figma~g2:figma-generate-diagram: Stage: diagramming in FigJam. Project fit: flowcharts, architecture, sequence, ERD, state, gantt, or timeline diagrams. Required tools: Figma MCP generate_diagram, load this skill before every call. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-use-figjam: this covers diagram types and Mermaid rules; use-figjam covers other FigJam writes. Not for: mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams (say so and skip the tool).
skills.figma~g2:figma-generate-library: Stage: design system build. Project fit: a codebase that should become a Figma design system (variables, tokens, components, variants, light and dark modes). Required tools: Figma MCP use_figma with figma-use loaded alongside. Model fit: any Claude model, larger task. Tie-breaker vs figma-generate-design: use this for tokens and reusable components; generate-design is for composed screens. Not for: a single screen with no new system work.
skills.figma~g2:figma-implement-motion: Stage: build motion. Project fit: animation from a Figma design to app code. Required tools: Figma MCP get_design_context or get_motion_context. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-use-motion: this writes app code from motion data; use-motion edits animation inside Figma. Not for: animating nodes inside Figma.
skills.figma~g2:figma-use-figjam: Stage: FigJam writes. Project fit: a FigJam board via use_figma. Required tools: Figma MCP use_figma, load figma-use alongside. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-use: this is the FigJam context; figma-use is the base for Design files. Diagram types go to figma-generate-diagram. Not for: Design or Slides files.
skills.figma~g2:figma-use-motion: Stage: animation inside Figma. Project fit: adding, editing, or inspecting keyframes, animation styles, easing, or timeline duration on a Figma node. Required tools: Figma MCP use_figma, load figma-use alongside. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-implement-motion: this edits motion in Figma; implement-motion writes app code. Not for: app code.
skills.figma~g2:figma-use-slides: Stage: Slides writes. Project fit: a Figma Slides file via use_figma. Required tools: Figma MCP use_figma, load figma-use alongside. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-use-figjam and figma-use: this is the Slides context only. Not for: Design or FigJam files.
skills.figma~g2:figma-generate-design: Stage: write to Figma. Project fit: a page, view, modal or multi-section layout built from code or a description into a Figma file. Required tools: Figma MCP use_figma, with figma-use loaded alongside. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker vs figma-generate-library: this assembles screens from existing system components; generate-library builds tokens and reusable components. Not for: a single component or tokens, or reading Figma into code (design-to-code).
skills.figma~g2:figma-use: Stage: foundation for every use_figma write or JavaScript read on a Figma Design file (create, edit, variables, components, auto-layout). Required tools: Figma MCP use_figma; load before the first call. Model fit: any Claude model. Tie-breaker: load alongside the context skill (use-figjam, use-slides, use-motion, generate-design, generate-library) when one applies. Not for: FigJam diagrams (generate-diagram).
